findings.title: Docker API answering without authentication
findings.description: The Docker Engine API answered a version request without credentials. Anyone on the LAN can run containers on this host.
findings.remediation: Bind the Docker API to localhost or a Unix socket, or require TLS client certificates (2376).
findings.unknown: Nothing beyond the version call was tried.

evidence.summary: GET /version returned Docker Engine version data

findings.title: Telnet login service answering
findings.description: The device answered as a Telnet server, so logins and sessions to it travel in cleartext.
findings.remediation: Disable Telnet and use SSH (port 22) with key-based auth instead.
findings.unknown: Whether logins are limited to trusted hosts, and how strong the accounts are.

findings.title: FTP server answering
findings.description: The device greeted as an FTP server. Plain FTP sends passwords and files in cleartext.
findings.remediation: Prefer SFTP/FTPS; disable anonymous FTP; restrict to trusted hosts.
findings.unknown: Whether anonymous login is allowed and whether FTPS is offered were not checked.

findings.title: TLS certificate expired
findings.description: TLS service on 192.0.2.9:443 presents a certificate that expired on 2026-08-01.
findings.remediation: Renew the certificate; prefer a privately trusted or publicly trusted cert for admin UIs.

findings.title: Telnet port open
findings.description: Port 23 is conventionally Telnet, which sends logins and sessions in cleartext.
findings.remediation: Disable Telnet and use SSH (port 22) with key-based auth instead.
findings.unknown: Only the TCP port answered. The software behind it, its version, and whether it asks for a login were not checked.

findings.title: SMB file sharing port open
findings.description: Port 445 is Windows/Samba file sharing. Normal for NAS boxes and PCs that share folders.
findings.remediation: Disable SMBv1; require signing; limit share permissions; patch the host.
findings.unknown: Share permissions, SMB version, and signing were not checked.

findings.title: Many services open
findings.description: Host 192.0.2.3 has 9 open services from the findings list — review which are needed.
findings.remediation: Close unused services; firewall management ports to trusted hosts only.
findings.unknown: Which of these services are intended.

findings.title: VNC screen sharing port open
findings.description: Port 5900 is VNC, which may use weak or no encryption depending on configuration.
findings.remediation: Tunnel VNC over SSH/VPN; require strong passwords; disable if unused.
findings.unknown: Whether a password or encryption is required was not checked.

findings.title: PostgreSQL port open
findings.description: A database reachable from the whole LAN is worth confirming as intended.
findings.remediation: Bind to localhost; use scram/password auth; restrict with firewall rules.
findings.unknown: Authentication settings (pg_hba.conf) were not checked.

findings.title: Remote Desktop (RDP) port open
findings.description: Port 3389 is Windows Remote Desktop, which gives full control of the machine to anyone who can log in.
findings.remediation: Restrict RDP to trusted hosts/VPN; enable NLA; use strong accounts or disable if unused.
findings.unknown: Whether Network Level Authentication is on and how strong the accounts are were not checked.

findings.title: Cleartext web page (HTTP)
findings.description: The device served a web page over unencrypted HTTP. Avoid logging in to admin pages over it.
findings.remediation: Prefer HTTPS; avoid sending credentials over HTTP; restrict admin UIs.

findings.title: Self-signed TLS certificate
findings.description: TLS service on 192.0.2.1:443 uses a self-signed certificate (CN unifi.local). Common on LAN gear, but browsers will warn.
findings.remediation: Replace with a cert from your internal CA or a public CA if the UI is shared; verify you trust this device.
findings.unknown: Whether this is the certificate you expect: compare its fingerprint with the device's settings page.

findings.title: RPCbind / portmapper open
findings.description: RPCbind advertises NFS and other Unix RPC services to the LAN.
findings.remediation: Disable unused RPC services; firewall 111; prefer NFS over authenticated, restricted mounts.

findings.remediation: Disable NetBIOS where unused; prefer SMB over 445 with signing; restrict with firewall rules.
